text: Ἀραβία, Arabia, the district south of Palestine.
gloss: Arabia, the district south of Palestine

text: Ἀράμ (Hebr.), Aram, son of Esrom and father of Aminadab.
gloss: Aram, son of Esrom and father of Aminadab

text: ἀργέω, I am idle (unemployed, without occupation) (generally, outside N.T., of necessity, and not blameworthily).
ἄργυρος (rare in papyri), silver as a metal (except Mt. x 9, where silver used as money).

Ἄρειος Πάγος (lit. Hill of Ares [the Athenian war-god, corresponding to Mars]), the Areopagus, a hill in Athens. As on this hill the Council of the Areopagus (ἡ ἐξ Ἀρείου Πάγου βουλή), the supreme court of Athens, had met in early times, the expression ὁ Ἄρειος Πάγος came to be used (as in Ac. xvii 19, 22) for the Council of the Areopagus, wheresoever it met.
gloss: the Areopagus, a hill in Athens

text: Ἀρεοπαγίτης, member of the Council of the Areopagus, an Areopagite.
gloss: member of the Council of the Areopagus, an Areopagite

note: headword printed ἀρέσκεια (accent differs from lemma)

text: Ἀρέτας (Ἁρέτας, for Ἁρέθας, Arabic Ḥāriṯā), Aretas, Aretas IV, King of the Nabataeans.
gloss: Aretas, Aretas IV, King of the Nabataeans
note: diacritics under H and t in Arabic Ḥāriṯā are tiny on the image (dot under H, line under t read)

text: (ἀρήν), a lamb: acc. pl. ἄρνας (Lk. x 3); the nom. (= ϝαρήν) is found only in early times, and its place is taken by ἀρνίον.
Ἀριμαθαία, Arimathaea, a place in Palestine, identical with Ramathaim, the birthplace of Samuel. Originally part of Samaria, it with its surrounding district was united to Judaea under the Maccabees.
Ἀρίσταρχος, Aristarchus, a Christian, belonging to Thessalonica in Macedonia.
gloss: Aristarchus, a Christian, belonging to Thessalonica

text: ἀριστερός, on the left hand: ἡ ἀριστερά (understand χείρ), Mt. vi 3; ἐξ ἀριστερῶν, on the left hand.
Ἀριστόβουλος, Aristobulus, a Christian in Rome.
ἀρκέω, (a) act. I am sufficient, I suffice; impers. John xiv 8; (b) mid. c. dat. I am content, satisfied (with).
ἄρκος (a later form of ἄρκτος), a bear.
ἁρμόζομαι, I fit, join (the middle indicating deep personal interest).
ἁρμός, a joint of the body.
ἁρπαγμός, either (a) snatching, robbery, the action of plundering, rapacity, self-aggrandizement, or (b) a thing to be snatched, plunder, prey, booty, a prize, spoil.
gloss: snatching, robbery, the action of plundering

text: ἅρπαξ, snatching, robbing, greedy: subst. swindler, extortioner, 1 Cor. v 10.
ἀρραβών (ἀραβών, a word of Semitic origin) (arra), an earnest, earnest-money, a large part of the payment, given in advance as a security that the whole will be paid afterwards.
ἄρρητος, not to be uttered (because too sacred), secret.
Ἀρτεμᾶς (a pet form of Ἀρτεμίδωρος), Artemas, a Christian in Rome.
Ἄρτεμις, Artemis, a goddess, worshipped principally at Ephesus, typifying fertility (she had no relation with the other Artemis, the maiden huntress, to whom corresponded the Latin Diana).
gloss: Artemis, a goddess, worshipped principally at Ephesus

text: ἀρτέμων, a foresail, set on the bow.
gloss: a foresail, set on the bow

text: Ἀρφαξάδ (Hebr.), Arphaxad, son of Shem, and father of Cainam.
gloss: Arphaxad, son of Shem, and father of Cainam

text: ἀρχάγγελος, a ruler of angels, a superior angel, an archangel.
gloss: a ruler of angels, a superior angel, an archangel

text: Ἀρχέλαος, Archelaus, Herod Archelaus, son and successor of Herod I, reigned over Judaea from 4 B.C. to A.D. 6 and died before A.D. 18.
gloss: Archelaus, Herod Archelaus, son and successor of Herod I

text: ἀρχιερατικός, high priestly, to which the chief priest belongs.
gloss: high priestly, to which the chief priest belongs

text: Ἄρχιππος, Archippus, a Christian of Colossae.
ἀρχιτελώνης, head of a custom-house, chief tax gatherer.
gloss: head of a custom-house, chief tax gatherer

text: ἀρχιτρίκλινος (arbiter bibendi), master of ceremonies at a dinner, master of the feast.
gloss: master of ceremonies at a dinner, master of the feast

text: Ἀσάφ (Hebr.), Asaph, Asa, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah about 900 B.C. for 41 years.
gloss: Asaph, Asa, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat

text: ἀσεβέω, (a) intr. I am impious, irreverent; (b) tr. I do impiously.
Ἀσήρ (Hebr.), Asher, one of the sons of Jacob, and founder of one of the Twelve Tribes.
gloss: Asher, one of the sons of Jacob

text: Ἀσιανός, belonging to the Roman province Asia.
gloss: belonging to the Roman province Asia

text: Ἀσιάρχης, Asiarch, an official connected with the worship of Rome and the Emperor in the Roman province Asia.
gloss: Asiarch, an official connected with the worship of Rome

text: ἀσιτία, either lack of corn, lack of food (the lit. meaning), or abstinence from food, loss of appetite, sea-sickness (the extended meaning).
gloss: lack of corn, lack of food

text: ἄσιτος, either without corn, without food, or sea-sick.
ἀσπίς, an asp (hooded-snake, cobra da capello).
ἀσσάριον (assarius, dimin. of as), a penny (1/16 of a δηνάριον and the tenth part of a drachma or franc).
note: fraction printed as a small built-up 1/16

text: Ἆσσος, Assos, a port of Mysia, in the Roman province Asia.
note: breathing/accent mark before capital Α is blurred; read as smooth breathing with circumflex (Ἆ)

text: ἀστατέω, I am unsettled, have no place of abode, lead a vagabond life.
gloss: I am unsettled, have no place of abode

text: ἀστεῖος (lit. belonging to the city: then witty, clever), elegant, pretty, fair, fine.
ἀστοχέω, I miss the mark, miss my aim, make a false aim.
gloss: I miss the mark, miss my aim, make a false aim

text: ἀστράπτω, I flash, (with, then like, lightning).
ἀσύνθετος, not covenanting, untrue to an agreement, treacherous.
gloss: not covenanting, untrue to an agreement, treacherous

text: Ἀσύνκριτος, Asyncritus, a Christian in Rome.
ἀσφάλεια, safety; security, reliability, Lk. i 4.
ἀσχημονέω, I am unseemly, I behave unbecomingly (or even dishonourably); perhaps, I consider (something) unseemly.
gloss: I am unseemly, I behave unbecomingly

text: ἀσχημοσύνη, unseemly behaviour, indecency, or concrete, an indecent (lewd) act.
ἀσώτως, prodigally: ζῶν ἀσώτως, with prodigal living (Field).
ἀτακτέω (lit. I march out of order; then I riot, I rebel), I am disorderly, I neglect my duty, I am careless (or idle) in habits.
gloss: I am disorderly, I neglect my duty

text: ἄτακτος (lit. out of order), disorderly, slack (in performance of duty).
ἀτάκτως, in a disorderly manner (see ἄτακτος, ἀτακτέω).
ἄτομος (lit. that cannot be cut), an indivisible part of time, a second.
gloss: an indivisible part of time, a second

text: ἄτοπος (lit. out of place, unusual, unbecoming), improper, unrighteous, perverse, froward: almost = evil, Ac. xxviii 6.
Ἀττάλεια, Attalia, the port of Perga in Pamphylia.
gloss: Attalia, the port of Perga in Pamphylia

text: αὐγάζω, I flash, gleam, appear white, bright (as in LXX), but perhaps, I see, I see clearly (as in classical poetry).
gloss: I flash, gleam, appear white, bright

text: Αὔγουστος, Augustus, a title conferred on the first Roman Emperor, C. Iulius Octauianus, denoting sanctity (almost divinity); grecized as Σεβαστός (q. v.).
gloss: Augustus, a title conferred on the first Roman Emperor
note: headword printed Αὔγουστος (accent differs from lemma)

text: αὐθεντέω (a colloquial word, from αὐθέντης, ‘master’, ‘autocrat’ [= αὐτός + root sen, ‘accomplish’, in ἁνύω]), I domineer over.
note: breathing on ἁνύω is poorly printed (read as rough); 'sen' read where OCR had 'sem'

text: αὐλίζομαι, I bivouac, I pass the night.
gloss: I bivouac, I pass the night

text: αὐτάρκης, self-sufficient, independent, contented (a literary use).
αὐτόχειρ (probably exclusively literary), with one's own hand.
αὐχέω (mostly in poetry), I speak with proud confidence of, I boast of.
gloss: I speak with proud confidence of, I boast of

text: αὐχμηρός (poetical, lit. dry and parched; then squalid and rough), dingy, dusky, obscure, dark, funereal.
ἄφεσις (from ἀφίημι) (remissio), a sending away, a letting go, a release; hence (cf. in inscriptions, remission from debt or punishment), remission, forgiveness.
note: current_text is the continuation (top of p. 51) of the entry ἄφεσις, which begins at the foot of p. 50; text given is the whole ἄφεσις entry. The page running head is ἁφή; the real ἁφή entry is entry 879

text: ἁφή, a band, fastening (hence, possibly, a ligament).
ἄφθαρτος, indestructible, imperishable, incorruptible; hence immortal.
ἀφθορία, (moral) incorruptness, incorruption, purity, freedom from taint.
gloss: incorruptness, incorruption, purity, freedom from taint

text: ἀφικνέομαι (in ordinary use very rare at this time), I arrive, reach.
ἀφιλάγαθος, not loving that which is good.
gloss: not loving that which is good

text: ἀφιλάργυρος, not loving money, not avaricious.

ἄφιξις, departure. (This is the sense required by Ac. xx 29, but as the word comes from ἀφικνέομαι, it ought to mean arrival. No certain parallel (except Josephus, Antiq. ii 18 fin., where = departure or journey) for this change of sense has been found.)
ἀφοράω (cf. ἀποβλέπω), I look away from (something else) to: ἀφίδω, Phil. ii 23, aspirated from ἀπίδω by analogy with ἀφοράω.
gloss: I look away from (something else) to

text: ἀφορμή (a) a starting, a start; (b) cause, occasion, opportunity.
ἀχειροποίητος (unknown outside N.T.), not made by hand, not handmade.
gloss: not made by hand, not handmade

text: Ἀχείμ (Hebr.), Acheim, son of Zadok and father of Eliud.
gloss: Acheim, son of Zadok and father of Eliud
note: headword printed Ἀχείμ; current_text was the wrong entry (Ἀχελδαμάχ), corrected to the Ἀχείμ entry just above it

text: ἀχρεόομαι (earlier ἀχρειόομαι) (lit. I become sour, I turn, of milk), I am good for nothing.
ἄχρηστος, unprofitable, useless (a play upon words, with ὀνήσιμος).
ἀψευδής, not guilty of falsehood, truthful.
ἄψινθος, wormwood; ὁ Ἄψινθος, a star.

Βάαλ (Bahal, properly Lord, and so not a proper name), Baal, a god worshipped by the Hebrews (in Rom. xi 4 fem., because Jews in reading substituted αἰσχύνη), being the highest god of all the West-Semitic peoples.
gloss: Baal, a god worshipped by the Hebrews
